sourceRange.text: 天命元年丙辰春正月壬申朔，上卽位，建元天命，定國號曰金。諸貝勒大臣上尊號曰覆育列國英明皇帝。命次子代善爲大貝勒，弟子阿敏爲二貝勒，五子莽古爾泰爲三貝勒，八子皇太極爲四貝勒。命額亦都、費英東、何和里、扈爾漢、安費揚古爲五大臣，同聽國政。諭以秉志公誠，勵精圖治。扈爾漢巡邊，執殺盜葠者五十餘人。明巡撫李維翰止我使者綱古里、方吉訥。乃取獄俘十人戮於境上，綱古里等得歸。

context.beforeSource: 於是歸徠日衆，疆域益廣，諸貝勒大臣乃再三勸進焉。

sourceRange.text: 天命十一年丙寅九月庚午朔，即位於瀋陽。詔以明年為天聰元年。初，太祖命上名，臆制之，後知漢稱儲君曰「皇太子」，蒙古嗣位者曰「黃台吉」，音並闇合。及即位，咸以為有天意焉。

manualTranslations.zh: 天命十一年丙寅九月庚午朔，即位於瀋陽。
manualTranslations.literal: On the new moon of the gengwu day in the ninth month of the bingyin year, the eleventh year of Tianming, he took the throne at Mukden.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the first day of the ninth month of the eleventh year of Tianming (bingyin), he took the throne at Mukden.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔以明年為天聰元年。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict declared that the coming year would be the first year of Tiancong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed that the next year would be the first year of Tiancong.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，太祖命上名，臆制之，後知漢稱儲君曰「皇太子」，蒙古嗣位者曰「黃台吉」，音並闇合。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, Taizu had given the Emperor a name of his own invention; later it was learned that the Han call the heir apparent "Crown Prince" and that Mongol successors to the throne are called "Huang Taiji" — the sounds all matched in secret.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, Nurhaci had invented a personal name for him; later they learned that Han call the heir apparent "Crown Prince" and that Mongol successors are styled "Huang Taiji"—the sounds secretly matched.

manualTranslations.zh: 及即位，咸以為有天意焉。
manualTranslations.literal: When he ascended the throne, all regarded it as Heaven's intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, everyone took it as a sign of Heaven's will.

sourceRange.text: 天聰元年春正月丙子，命二貝勒阿敏，貝勒濟爾哈朗、阿濟格、杜度、岳言乇、碩托率兵征朝鮮。上曰：「朝鮮累世得罪，今明毛文龍近彼海島，納我叛民，宜兩圖之。」復遣方吉納、溫塔石遺書明袁崇煥，言興師由七大恨，並約其議和，及每歲餽報之數。

manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong, in the first month of spring, on the day bingzi, he ordered Second Beile Amin and the beile Jirhalang, Ajige, Dudu, Yuetuo, and Šoto to lead troops against Korea.

manualTranslations.zh: 上曰：「朝鮮累世得罪，今明毛文龍近彼海島，納我叛民，宜兩圖之。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor said: "Korea has offended generation after generation; now the Ming Mao Wenlong is near their island harbors, receiving our defectors — both should be dealt with."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huang Taiji declared: "Korea has given offense for generations. Now the Ming general Mao Wenlong holds an island nearby and shelters our deserters—we should settle both accounts."

manualTranslations.zh: 復遣方吉納、溫塔石遺書明袁崇煥，言興師由七大恨，並約其議和，及每歲餽報之數。
manualTranslations.literal: He again dispatched Fangjina and Wentashi with a letter to Yuan Chonghuan of the Ming, stating that the campaign arose from the Seven Grievances, and also proposing terms for peace and the yearly gifts and returns.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He again sent Fangjina and Wentashi with a letter to the Ming commander Yuan Chonghuan, citing the Seven Grievances as the cause of arms and proposing peace talks along with the annual tribute exchange.

manualTranslations.zh: 天命元年，太祖以上為和碩貝勒，與大貝勒代善、二貝勒阿敏、三貝勒莽古爾泰為四大貝勒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Tianming, Taizu made the Emperor a hošo-i beile; together with Great Beile Daisan, Second Beile Amin, and Third Beile Manggūltai he formed the Four Great Beile.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianming, Nurhaci made Huang Taiji a hošo-i beile, joining Great Beile Daisan, Second Beile Amin, and Third Beile Manggūltai as the Four Great Beile.

manualTranslations.zh: 上居四，稱四貝勒。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor held the fourth rank and was styled Fourth Beile.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He held the fourth place among them and was known as Fourth Beile.

sourceRange.text: 崇德元年夏四月乙酉，祭告天地，行受尊號禮，定有天下之號曰大清，改元崇德，群臣上尊號曰寬溫仁聖皇帝，受朝賀。始定祀天太牢用熟薦。遣官以建太廟追尊列祖祭告山陵。丙戌，追尊始祖為澤王，高祖為慶王，曾祖為昌王，祖為福王，考諡曰承天廣運聖德神功肇紀立極仁孝武皇帝，廟號太祖，陵曰福陵；妣諡曰孝慈昭憲純德貞順成天育聖武皇后。追贈族祖禮敦巴圖魯為武功郡王，追封功臣費英東為直義公，額亦都為弘毅公，配享。丁亥，群臣上表賀。諭曰：「朕以涼德，恐負眾望。爾諸臣宜同心匡輔，各共厥職，正己率屬，克殫忠誠，立綱陳紀，撫民恤眾，使君明臣良，政治咸熙，庶克荷天之休命。」群臣頓首曰：「聖諭及此，國家之福也。」以受尊號禮成，大赦。己丑，多濟里、扈習征瓦爾喀師還，賞賚有差。朝鮮使臣歸國。初，上受尊號，朝鮮使臣羅德憲、李廓獨不拜。上曰：「彼國王將構怨，欲朕殺其使臣以為詞耳，其釋之。」至是遣歸，以書諭朝鮮國王責之，命送子弟為質。丁酉，敘功，封大貝勒代善為和碩兄禮親王，貝勒濟爾哈朗為和碩鄭親王，多爾袞為和碩睿親王，多鐸為和碩豫親王，豪格為和碩肅親王，岳託為和碩成親王，阿濟格為多羅武英郡王，杜度為多羅安平貝勒，阿巴泰為多羅饒餘貝勒；諸蒙古貝勒巴達禮為和碩土謝圖親王，吳克善為和碩卓禮克圖親王，固倫額駙額哲為和碩親王，布塔齊為多羅札薩克圖郡王，滿硃習禮為多羅巴圖魯郡王，袞出斯巴圖魯為多羅達爾漢郡王，孫杜棱為多羅杜棱郡王，固倫額駙班第為多羅郡王，孔果爾為冰圖王，東為多羅達爾漢戴青，俄木布為多羅達爾漢卓禮克圖，古魯思轄布為多羅杜棱，單把為達爾漢，耿格爾為多羅貝勒，孔有德為恭順王，耿仲明為懷順王，尚可喜為智順王。辛丑，朝鮮使臣置我書於通遠堡，不以歸。札福尼征瓦爾喀師還。

context.afterSource: 五月丙午，以希福為內弘文院大學士，范文程、鮑承先俱為內秘書院大學士，剛林為內國史院大學士。

manualTranslations.zh: 崇德元年夏四月乙酉，祭告天地，行受尊號禮，定有天下之號曰大清，改元崇德，群臣上尊號曰寬溫仁聖皇帝，受朝賀。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, in the fourth month of summer, on the day yiyou, heaven and earth were notified in sacrifice; the ceremony of receiving the honorific title was performed; the name of possessing All-under-Heaven was fixed as Great Qing; the era name was changed to Chongde; the assembled ministers presented the honorific title Broad, Gentle, Benevolent, and Sagely Emperor; and court congratulations were received.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde, on yiyou day in the fourth month of summer, sacrifices were offered to heaven and earth and the ceremony of receiving the honorific title was performed. The realm was named Great Qing, the era was changed to Chongde, the ministers presented the title Broad, Gentle, Benevolent, and Sagely Emperor, and court congratulations were received.

manualTranslations.zh: 始定祀天太牢用熟薦。
manualTranslations.literal: It was first fixed that the great offering in sacrifices to heaven should use cooked offerings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It was first ordained that heaven sacrifices should use cooked offerings in the great victim rite.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣官以建太廟追尊列祖祭告山陵。
manualTranslations.literal: Officials were dispatched to build the Imperial Ancestral Temple, posthumously honor the successive ancestors, and offer sacrifice and notification at the imperial tombs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Officials were sent to build the Imperial Ancestral Temple, posthumously honor the founding ancestors, and offer sacrifice at the imperial tombs.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙戌，追尊始祖為澤王，高祖為慶王，曾祖為昌王，祖為福王，考諡曰承天廣運聖德神功肇紀立極仁孝武皇帝，廟號太祖，陵曰福陵；
manualTranslations.literal: On bingxu day the founding ancestor was posthumously honored as Prince Ze, the great-grandfather as Prince Qing, the grandfather as Prince Chang, the father as Prince Fu, and the father was given the posthumous title Emperor who Receives Heaven, Extends Fortune, Sages in Virtue, Divine in Achievement, Begins the Record, Establishes the Pole, Benevolent, Filial, and Martial; his temple name was Taizu, and his tomb was called Fuling;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingxu day the founding ancestor was posthumously honored as Prince Ze, the great-grandfather as Prince Qing, the grandfather as Prince Chang, and the father as Prince Fu. The father received the posthumous title Emperor who Receives Heaven, Extends Fortune, Sages in Virtue, Divine in Achievement, Begins the Record, Establishes the Pole, Benevolent, Filial, and Martial; his temple name was Taizu, and his tomb was called Fuling;

manualTranslations.zh: 妣諡曰孝慈昭憲純德貞順成天育聖武皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: The mother was given the posthumous title Empress Filial, Kind, Illustrious in Statutes, Pure in Virtue, Chaste and Obedient, Nurtured by Heaven, Sagely and Martial.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The mother received the posthumous title Empress Filial, Kind, Illustrious in Statutes, Pure in Virtue, Chaste and Obedient, Nurtured by Heaven, Sagely and Martial.

manualTranslations.zh: 追贈族祖禮敦巴圖魯為武功郡王，追封功臣費英東為直義公，額亦都為弘毅公，配享。
manualTranslations.literal: The clan ancestor Lidun Batulu was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wugong Commandery; the meritorious ministers Fiyanggū and Eidu were posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhiyi and Duke of Hongyi, with attendant sacrifice at the temple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The clan ancestor Lidun Batulu was posthumously made Prince of Wugong Commandery; the meritorious ministers Fiyanggū and Eidu were posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhiyi and Duke of Hongyi, with attendant sacrifice at the temple.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁亥，群臣上表賀。
manualTranslations.literal: On dinghai day the assembled ministers submitted memorials of congratulation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dinghai day the ministers submitted memorials of congratulation.

manualTranslations.zh: 諭曰：「朕以涼德，恐負眾望。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict said: "I am of meager virtue and fear I may fail the people's hopes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "My virtue is slight, and I fear I may disappoint the people's hopes.

manualTranslations.zh: 爾諸臣宜同心匡輔，各共厥職，正己率屬，克殫忠誠，立綱陳紀，撫民恤眾，使君明臣良，政治咸熙，庶克荷天之休命。」
manualTranslations.literal: You ministers should with one heart assist and support me, each fulfill your duties, correct yourselves and lead your subordinates, fully devote your loyalty, establish standards and set forth regulations, comfort the people and show compassion to the multitude, so that the ruler is enlightened and the ministers worthy and government is altogether flourishing, and thus we may bear heaven's gracious mandate."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You ministers should assist me with one heart, each fulfill your office, correct yourselves and lead your subordinates, devote your loyalty fully, establish standards and set forth regulations, comfort the people and show them compassion, so that ruler and ministers are worthy and government flourishes, and we may bear heaven's gracious mandate."

manualTranslations.zh: 群臣頓首曰：「聖諭及此，國家之福也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The assembled ministers bowed their heads and said: "That the sacred instruction reaches this point is the fortune of the state."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ministers bowed and said: "That Your Majesty's sacred instruction reaches this point is the fortune of the state."

manualTranslations.zh: 以受尊號禮成，大赦。
manualTranslations.literal: Because the ceremony of receiving the honorific title was completed, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because the ceremony of receiving the honorific title was completed, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

manualTranslations.zh: 己丑，多濟里、扈習征瓦爾喀師還，賞賚有差。
manualTranslations.literal: On jichou day the armies of Doroji and Huxi, campaigning against the Warka, returned; rewards and gifts were granted in differing measure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jichou day Doroji and Huxi returned from the Warka campaign; rewards were granted in differing measure.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝鮮使臣歸國。
manualTranslations.literal: The Korean envoys returned to their country.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Korean envoys returned home.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，上受尊號，朝鮮使臣羅德憲、李廓獨不拜。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor received the honorific title, the Korean envoys Luo Dexian and Li Kuo alone did not perform the bow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Emperor received the honorific title, the Korean envoys Luo Dexian and Li Kuo alone refused to bow.

manualTranslations.zh: 上曰：「彼國王將構怨，欲朕殺其使臣以為詞耳，其釋之。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor said: "That country's king intends to breed resentment and wants me to kill his envoys so as to have a pretext; release them."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Their king means to breed resentment and wants me to kill his envoys as a pretext; release them."

manualTranslations.zh: 至是遣歸，以書諭朝鮮國王責之，命送子弟為質。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time they were sent back; a letter was sent instructing the king of Korea and rebuking him, ordering that sons and younger brothers be sent as hostages.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At this time they were sent home with a letter rebuking the king of Korea and ordering that sons and younger brothers be sent as hostages.

sourceRange.text: 嘉慶元年六月，滕縣大雨如注七晝夜。二年六月，武進大風雨，拔木壞屋。七月，寧都霪雨，壞民居。四年二月，監利大雨如注，平地水深尺許。七月，文登大風雨，傷稼。五年六月，金華大雨三日，傷稼。六年六月，邢台、懷來、寧津大雨數晝夜，壞廬舍；清苑、新樂霪雨四十餘日。七年四月，義烏霪雨，禾盡淹沒。九年三月，桐鄉恒雨，傷麥。五月，嘉興、蘇州霪雨，傷稼。十年三月，嘉興、石門恒雨，傷麥。六月，黃岩大風雨，損稼。十一年夏，樂亭霪雨四十餘日。十三年五月，嘉興、石門大風雨，害稼。閏五月，新城大雨水，湖州霪雨。秋，漢陽霪雨彌月。十五年夏，臨邑霪雨四十餘日。十六年三月，永嘉霪雨匝月。七月，棲霞霪雨四十餘日。九月，榮成霪雨害稼。十七年春，嘉興、石門、桐鄉霪雨傷麥。十八年秋，東阿、曹縣霪雨四十餘日，田禾盡傷。十九年秋，漢陽霪雨傷稼。二十一年夏，滕縣大雨，平地水深數尺。二十三年五月二十日夜，濟南大雨水，壞城垣廬舍，民多溺死。六月，文登大雨，平地水深數尺，民多溺死。八月十三日，永嘉大雨如注十晝夜，平地水深數尺。二十四年六月，文登大風雨，害稼。二十五年七月，新城大雨九日，平地水深丈餘；宣平霪雨，壞田禾。道光元年七月，涇州霪雨，衝沒橋梁田廬人畜。八月，臨邑霪雨連旬。二年五月，莘縣霪雨傷稼。八月，章丘、東阿霪雨四十餘日，壞田廬禾稼。三年三月，湖州霪雨，至五月不止；昌平霪雨傷麥；內丘大雨，三旬始止。四月，嵊縣霪雨，至九月始止。五月，金華、永嘉霪雨害稼；禮縣暴雨，漂沒民舍。七月，青浦霪雨兩月；泰州大雨，平地水深數尺，禾稼盡淹。四年二月，德州霪雨。五年八月，貴陽大雨，二十日始止。六年六月，宜昌大雨連綿，十日不止，損田禾。七年夏，恩施霪雨傷稼。八年七月，武城霪雨。十年五月，通山，崇陽霪雨連旬，漂沒田廬甚多。六月，恩施霪雨傷稼。八月，宣平大雨如注，民舍盡漂沒。十一年五月，永嘉大雨水，歉收；江夏霪雨彌月。六月，宜城、穀城霪雨二十餘日，傷稼。七月，菏澤、滕縣霪雨百餘日，平地水深數尺；曹縣大雨，水深二尺。十二年，光化霪雨，自六月至八月，禾苗盡傷；宜城大雨，晝夜不絕；定遠廳、保康霪雨兩月。七月，鄖陽大雨七晝夜，壞官署民房大半。冬，房縣霪雨害稼。十三年夏，湖州霪雨害稼。十四年四月，咸寧大風雨，拔木壞房。七月，麗水大風雨，平地水深數尺。十五年夏，即墨霪雨傷稼，文登、榮成大雨六十餘日。八月，宜城霪雨傷稼。十七年五月，崇陽、宜城霪雨害稼。十八年六月，益都、臨淄大雨水。十九年春，棲霞霪雨，南樂大雨。四月，招遠大雨十餘日；榮成大雨，至七月不止。九月，武進恒雨傷稼。二十年五月，邢台大雨，平地水深三尺。六月，平穀霪雨匝月不止。二十一年二月，武進恒雨傷麥。二十二年七月，麗水大雨，漂沒田廬。冬至夜，滕縣大雨如注。二十三年五月，平度霪雨傷田禾。二十四年七月初九日，嵊縣大風雨，溺死男婦七十餘人。冬，鬆陽大雨連旬，壞田舍無數。二十五年春，棗陽霪雨八十餘日。六月，滕縣大雨，平地水深數尺，人多溺死。二十六年五月，東平大雨害稼。六月，樂平霪雨。二十八年，潛江自二月至七月雨不止。六月，光化大雨，平地水深數尺，三月始退，溺斃人無算；保康霪雨兩月，壞田廬無算。七月十四日，永嘉大風雨，壞孔子廟及縣署。十九日，景寧大風雨三晝夜，壞田廬無算。二十九年六月，樂亭大雨傷禾稼。七月，青浦霪雨五十日，湖州霪雨傷禾。三十年五月二十五日，兩當暴雨，漂沒人畜。咸豐元年六月，禮縣霪雨四十餘日，傷禾。二年，青縣大雨傷禾。三年四月，靜海霪雨害稼。六月，永嘉、青田、景寧霪雨十晝夜；保康大雨十六日，漂沒田舍甚多；房縣霪雨七晝夜不止，壞田舍無算。七月，宜城大雨匝月，壞城垣一百五丈；遠州霪雨害稼。四年夏，湖州霪雨。五年七月初十日，景寧大雨如注，田廬盡壞。六年六月，昌平大雨傷稼。七年春，崇陽霪雨。八年四月，海囗縣大雨損禾苗。九年五月，蘇州大雨傷禾。十年二月，蘇州霪雨閱月。六月，寧津、東光大雨傷稼。十一年十一月，羅田大雨傷禾。同治元年七月，蓬萊、黃縣、福山、招遠、萊陽、寧海大雨連綿，禾稼盡淹。二年春，應城霪雨傷麥。五月，青縣大雨傷禾。三年六月初十日，定海暴風疾雨，壞各埠船，溺死兵民無數。四年六月至七月，萊陽大雨，平地水深七八尺，禾稼淹沒，房舍傾圮無算。五年秋，魚台霪雨，水深數尺，傷禾稼。六年八月，鄖陽霪雨三晝夜，壞官署民房甚多。七年五月，皋蘭、金縣大雨，至七月乃止。秋，景寧大雨，傾沒田廬無算。八年春，江夏霪雨損麥。四月，嵊縣大雨，壞田廬。九年六月，潛江霪雨傷稼。十年七月，東光、新樂、曲陽霪雨十餘日。十一年五月，東平霪雨害稼。十一月，青縣大雨害稼。十二年七月，太平大風雨，壞城垣數十丈，民房數百間。八月，化平廳霪雨不止，壞民舍。光緒元年六月，日照大風雨，平地水深數尺。二年六月初八日，黃岩大風雨，拔木壞屋，田禾淹沒殆盡。三年六月，高陵大雨如注，平地水深三尺，田禾盡沒。四年九月，東平大雨傷禾稼。五年五月，登州各屬大雨四十餘日。六月二十一日，永嘉大風雨，壞官廳民居。八月，莘縣霪雨十日方止。六年三月，福山大雨。七年秋，灤州霪雨連旬。八年秋，宜城霪雨傷禾稼。冬，均州霪雨彌月。九年六月，化平廳大雨，水深四五尺，傷禾稼。十年八月，太平大雨，衝沒廬舍。十二年七月十四日，太平大風雨，二十日始止。十三年閏四月，德安大雨三日，水高五六尺。十五年七月二十六日夜，德安大雨如注，城崩百四十餘丈，淹斃男婦七十餘人。十六年六月，山丹驟雨壞城郭。二十二年春，寧津大雨壞民居。二十五年七月，秦安大雨連旬。二十七年七月，山丹大雨，平地水深數尺。雍正三年七月，靈川五都廖家塘有村民同眾入山砍竹不歸，一百四十餘日始抵家，所言多不經。道光十七年，崇陽鄉民好服尖頭帽鞋，站步不穩，識者謂之服妖。順治二年十二月，上海小南門薑姓家雞翼下各生一爪。三年八月，揭陽牝雞鳴數日乃已。四年四月，淄川民間訛言雞兩翅生骨，食之殺人，驗之果然。五月，忠州民家殺雞，腹內有一嬰兒；漢陽雞翅生爪。五年，崇明民家雞翼中生爪；巫山民間雞翅端皆生一爪如距；杭州民家雞生四足；湖州民家雞生四翼，能飛。十一年，合肥鄭家莊產一雞，三嘴、三眼、三翼、三足，色黃，比三日死。十六年，崇明民家雄雞生二卵。十八年，鎮澤民家雄雞生卵。康熙十一年，廣平民家抱一雛雞，四足四翼。十二年，平湖民家雞生四足四翼。二十二年，迎春鄉民間雌雞化為雄。二十三年，麻城民田姓家雞生一卵，膜內皆有紋，其色朱；後七日又生一卵，有圖；又數日，毛成五色，飛去。雍正二年，麻城雞翅遍生人指。五年，通州雌雞化為雄。乾隆三十九年冬，慶元雄雞自斷其尾。六十年，貴陽民家雄雞生二卵，色赤甚鮮。嘉慶十一年，樂清民家雞生四足。十七年，宜昌民間雞生四足，後二足微短，行不著地；又有三足者，其一生於尾下，如鼎足然。道光元年秋，青浦民家雞翼兩旁生爪；湖州民家雞兩翅皆生五爪，飛去；永嘉雞翅生爪，食之殺人。十二年，永嘉民家雞四足，不能啼。二十二年，良鄉民家牝雞化為雄，能鳴，無距。三十年六月，蘄水縣民家雌雞化為雄，冠距儼然，唯啼聲微弱。咸豐五年，隨州民家雄雞生卵。同治元年六月，定遠廳民家雞生三足。六年，鍾祥民家雛雞生三翅。光緒九年，興山民家雌雞化為雄。三十年，寧州民家雞生三足，後一足微短，行不著地。康熙二十年五月，巴東鼠食麥，色赤，尾大；江陵鼠災，食禾殆盡。二十一年，西寧鼠食禾。二十二年夏，崇陽田鼠結巢於禾麻之上。二十八年，黃岡鼠食禾，及秋，化為魚。二十九年，孝感鼠食稼。四十二年，西鄉、定遠廳遍地生五色鼠。四十七年，黃濟鼠食禾。四十八年七月，崖州有鼠千萬啣尾渡江。五十二年五月，高淳、丹陽有鼠無數，食禾殆盡。六十一年夏，延安田鼠食稼。秋，安定黑鼠為災，食禾殆盡，有鄉民掘地得一鼠，身後半蝦蟆形，疑其所化也；清澗黃鼠食苗殆盡；葭州田鼠食苗。雍正五年十一月，銅陵群鼠銜尾渡江。乾隆元年，文縣鼠害稼。四年四月，什邡縣白鼠晝見羅寺經堂中，異香滿室。秋，彭澤群鼠銜尾渡江，食禾。十四年二月，中衛田鼠食麥。十八年，池州田鼠叢生，忽入水化為魚。二十五年五月，池州田鼠叢生，有赤鷹來食之，遂滅。道光四年，高淳鼠食麥。二十八年五月，沔陽常平倉忽有鼠數千頭在梁上，移時方散。咸豐元年六月，德化群鼠銜尾渡江。四年，襄陽群鼠食禾。同治七年，山丹田鼠食苗。九年二月，皋蘭土塊化為鼠。

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉慶元年六月，滕縣大雨如注七晝夜。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of Jiaqing 1, Teng County had rain pouring down in torrents for seven days and nights.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jiaqing 1 (1796), torrential rain lashed Teng County for seven days and nights.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年六月，武進大風雨，拔木壞屋。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, Wujin had a great wind and rain, uprooting trees and destroying houses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jiaqing 2 (1797), a violent storm at Wujin uprooted trees and destroyed houses.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，寧都霪雨，壞民居。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Ningdu had incessant rain, destroying civilian dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, incessant rain at Ningdu destroyed many homes.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年二月，監利大雨如注，平地水深尺許。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, Jianli had rain pouring down in torrents, and the level ground stood about a foot deep in water.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jiaqing 4 (1799), torrential rain at Jianli left the flatlands about a foot deep in water.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，文登大風雨，傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Wendeng had a great wind and rain, harming the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, a violent storm at Wendeng damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年六月，金華大雨三日，傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, Jinhua had heavy rain for three days, harming the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jiaqing 5 (1800), three days of heavy rain at Jinhua damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年六月，邢台、懷來、寧津大雨數晝夜，壞廬舍；
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year, Xingtai, Huailai, and Ningjin had heavy rain for several days and nights, destroying dwellings;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jiaqing 6 (1801), several days and nights of heavy rain at Xingtai, Huailai, and Ningjin wrecked countless dwellings;

manualTranslations.zh: 清苑、新樂霪雨四十餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: Qingyuan and Xinle had incessant rain for more than forty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qingyuan and Xinle endured incessant rain for more than forty days.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年四月，義烏霪雨，禾盡淹沒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year, Yiwu had incessant rain, and the grain was entirely submerged.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Jiaqing 7 (1802), incessant rain at Yiwu wholly submerged the standing grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 九年三月，桐鄉恒雨，傷麥。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year, Tongxiang had persistent rain, harming the wheat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month of Jiaqing 9 (1804), persistent rain at Tongxiang ruined the wheat.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月，嘉興、蘇州霪雨，傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month, Jiaxing and Suzhou had incessant rain, harming the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, incessant rain at Jiaxing and Suzhou damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十年三月，嘉興、石門恒雨，傷麥。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year, Jiaxing and Shimen had persistent rain, harming the wheat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month of Jiaqing 10 (1805), persistent rain at Jiaxing and Shimen ruined the wheat.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，黃岩大風雨，損稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Huangyan had a great wind and rain, damaging the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, a violent storm at Huangyan damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一年夏，樂亭霪雨四十餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the eleventh year, Laoting had incessant rain for more than forty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jiaqing 11 (1806), Laoting endured incessant rain for more than forty days.

manualTranslations.zh: 十三年五月，嘉興、石門大風雨，害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year, Jiaxing and Shimen had a great wind and rain, ruining the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jiaqing 13 (1808), a violent storm at Jiaxing and Shimen ruined the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 閏五月，新城大雨水，湖州霪雨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month, Xincheng had great rain and water, and Huzhou had incessant rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month, flooding at Xincheng and incessant rain at Huzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋，漢陽霪雨彌月。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn, Hanyang had incessant rain for a full month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That autumn, Hanyang saw rain that lasted a full month without letup.

manualTranslations.zh: 十五年夏，臨邑霪雨四十餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the fifteenth year, Linyi had incessant rain for more than forty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jiaqing 15 (1810), Linyi endured incessant rain for more than forty days.

manualTranslations.zh: 十六年三月，永嘉霪雨匝月。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month of the sixteenth year, Yongjia had incessant rain for a full month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month of Jiaqing 16 (1811), Yongjia endured a full month of incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，棲霞霪雨四十餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Qixia had incessant rain for more than forty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Qixia saw incessant rain for more than forty days.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，榮成霪雨害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month, Rongcheng had incessant rain that ruined the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, incessant rain at Rongcheng ruined the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十七年春，嘉興、石門、桐鄉霪雨傷麥。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year, Jiaxing, Shimen, and Tongxiang had incessant rain that harmed the wheat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jiaqing 17 (1812), incessant rain at Jiaxing, Shimen, and Tongxiang ruined the wheat.

manualTranslations.zh: 十八年秋，東阿、曹縣霪雨四十餘日，田禾盡傷。
manualTranslations.literal: In the autumn of the eighteenth year, Dong'e and Caoxian had incessant rain for more than forty days, and the field grain was entirely harmed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Jiaqing 18 (1813), more than forty days of incessant rain at Dong'e and Caoxian wholly ruined the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十九年秋，漢陽霪雨傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the autumn of the nineteenth year, Hanyang had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Jiaqing 19 (1814), incessant rain at Hanyang damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十一年夏，滕縣大雨，平地水深數尺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-first year, Teng County had heavy rain, and the level ground stood several feet deep in water.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jiaqing 21 (1816), heavy rain at Teng County left the flatlands several feet deep in floodwater.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十三年五月二十日夜，濟南大雨水，壞城垣廬舍，民多溺死。
manualTranslations.literal: On the night of the twentieth day of the fifth month of the twenty-third year, Jinan had great rain and water, destroying city walls and dwellings, and many people drowned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the night of the twentieth day of the fifth month of Jiaqing 23 (1818), flooding at Jinan destroyed walls and dwellings, and many people drowned.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，文登大雨，平地水深數尺，民多溺死。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Wendeng had heavy rain, the level ground stood several feet deep in water, and many people drowned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, heavy rain at Wendeng left the flatlands several feet deep, and many people drowned.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月十三日，永嘉大雨如注十晝夜，平地水深數尺。
manualTranslations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the eighth month, Yongjia had rain pouring down in torrents for ten days and nights, and the level ground stood several feet deep in water.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the eighth month, torrential rain at Yongjia lasted ten days and nights and left the flatlands several feet deep in water.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十四年六月，文登大風雨，害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-fourth year, Wendeng had a great wind and rain, ruining the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jiaqing 24 (1819), a violent storm at Wendeng ruined the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十五年七月，新城大雨九日，平地水深丈餘；
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year, Xincheng had heavy rain for nine days, and the level ground stood more than a zhang deep in water;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jiaqing 25 (1820), nine days of heavy rain at Xincheng left the flatlands more than a zhang deep;

manualTranslations.zh: 宣平霪雨，壞田禾。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuanping had incessant rain that destroyed field grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Incessant rain at Xuanping destroyed the standing crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 道光元年七月，涇州霪雨，衝沒橋梁田廬人畜。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of Daoguang 1, Jingzhou had incessant rain, washing away and submerging bridges, fields, dwellings, people, and livestock.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Daoguang 1 (1821), incessant rain at Jingzhou washed away bridges, fields, dwellings, people, and livestock alike.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月，臨邑霪雨連旬。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, Linyi had incessant rain for successive ten-day periods.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Linyi was soaked by weeks of incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年五月，莘縣霪雨傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, Shen County had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Daoguang 2 (1822), incessant rain at Shen County damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月，章丘、東阿霪雨四十餘日，壞田廬禾稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, Zhangqiu and Dong'e had incessant rain for more than forty days, destroying fields, dwellings, and grain crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, more than forty days of incessant rain at Zhangqiu and Dong'e destroyed fields, homes, and crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年三月，湖州霪雨，至五月不止；
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month of the third year, Huzhou had incessant rain, continuing until the fifth month without cease;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month of Daoguang 3 (1823), incessant rain at Huzhou did not stop until the fifth month;

manualTranslations.zh: 昌平霪雨傷麥；
manualTranslations.literal: Changping had incessant rain that harmed the wheat;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Incessant rain at Changping ruined the wheat;

manualTranslations.zh: 內丘大雨，三旬始止。
manualTranslations.literal: Neiqiu had heavy rain, ceasing only after thirty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heavy rain at Neiqiu lasted thirty days before it stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 四月，嵊縣霪雨，至九月始止。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month, Sheng County had incessant rain, ceasing only in the ninth month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, incessant rain at Sheng County did not stop until the ninth month.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月，金華、永嘉霪雨害稼；
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month, Jinhua and Yongjia had incessant rain that ruined the crops;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, incessant rain at Jinhua and Yongjia ruined the crops;

manualTranslations.zh: 禮縣暴雨，漂沒民舍。
manualTranslations.literal: Li County had a violent rainstorm, washing away and submerging civilian dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A violent rainstorm at Li County washed away and submerged many homes.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，青浦霪雨兩月；
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Qingpu had incessant rain for two months;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Qingpu endured two months of incessant rain;

manualTranslations.zh: 泰州大雨，平地水深數尺，禾稼盡淹。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizhou had heavy rain, the level ground stood several feet deep in water, and the grain crops were entirely flooded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heavy rain at Taizhou left the flatlands several feet deep and wholly submerged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年二月，德州霪雨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, Dezhou had incessant rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Daoguang 4 (1824), Dezhou was battered by incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年八月，貴陽大雨，二十日始止。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year, Guiyang had heavy rain, ceasing only after twenty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Daoguang 5 (1825), heavy rain at Guiyang lasted twenty days before it stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年六月，宜昌大雨連綿，十日不止，損田禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year, Yichang had heavy rain continuously, not stopping for ten days, damaging field grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Daoguang 6 (1826), ten days of unbroken heavy rain at Yichang damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年夏，恩施霪雨傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year, Enshi had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Daoguang 7 (1827), incessant rain at Enshi damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 八年七月，武城霪雨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, Wucheng had incessant rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Daoguang 8 (1828), Wucheng endured incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 十年五月，通山，崇陽霪雨連旬，漂沒田廬甚多。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year, Tongshan and Chongyang had incessant rain for successive ten-day periods, washing away and submerging a great many fields and dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Daoguang 10 (1830), weeks of incessant rain at Tongshan and Chongyang washed away a great many fields and dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，恩施霪雨傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Enshi had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, incessant rain at Enshi damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月，宣平大雨如注，民舍盡漂沒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, Xuanping had rain pouring down in torrents, and civilian dwellings were entirely washed away and submerged.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, torrential rain at Xuanping wholly washed away and submerged homes.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一年五月，永嘉大雨水，歉收；
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year, Yongjia had great rain and water, and the harvest was poor;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Daoguang 11 (1831), flooding at Yongjia brought a poor harvest;

manualTranslations.zh: 江夏霪雨彌月。
manualTranslations.literal: Jiangxia had incessant rain for a full month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiangxia saw rain that lasted a full month without letup.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，宜城、穀城霪雨二十餘日，傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Yicheng and Gucheng had incessant rain for more than twenty days, harming the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Daoguang 11 (1831), Yicheng and Gucheng endured incessant rain for more than twenty days, damaging the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，菏澤、滕縣霪雨百餘日，平地水深數尺；
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Heze and Teng County had incessant rain for more than a hundred days, and on level ground the water stood several feet deep;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Daoguang 11 (1831), Heze and Teng County were deluged by incessant rain for more than a hundred days until the flatlands stood several feet deep in water;

manualTranslations.zh: 曹縣大雨，水深二尺。
manualTranslations.literal: Cao County had heavy rain, and the water stood two feet deep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Cao County heavy rain left the water two feet deep.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二年，光化霪雨，自六月至八月，禾苗盡傷；
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth year, Guanghua had incessant rain from the sixth month to the eighth month, and the grain seedlings were entirely harmed;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12 (1832), Guanghua suffered incessant rain from the sixth month through the eighth month, and the grain seedlings were entirely ruined;

manualTranslations.zh: 宜城大雨，晝夜不絕；
manualTranslations.literal: Yicheng had heavy rain that did not cease day or night;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Yicheng heavy rain fell without cease day or night;

manualTranslations.zh: 定遠廳、保康霪雨兩月。
manualTranslations.literal: Dingyuan Subprefecture and Baokang had incessant rain for two months.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dingyuan Subprefecture and Baokang saw incessant rain for two months.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，鄖陽大雨七晝夜，壞官署民房大半。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Yunyang had heavy rain for seven days and nights, and more than half the official offices and private dwellings were destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Daoguang 12 (1832), seven days and nights of heavy rain at Yunyang destroyed more than half the government offices and private dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬，房縣霪雨害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter, Fang County had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the winter of Daoguang 12 (1832), incessant rain at Fang County damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十三年夏，湖州霪雨害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the thirteenth year, Huzhou had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Daoguang 13 (1833), incessant rain at Huzhou damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十四年四月，咸寧大風雨，拔木壞房。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year, Xianning had great wind and rain that uprooted trees and destroyed houses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Daoguang 14 (1834), violent wind and rain at Xianning uprooted trees and destroyed houses.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，麗水大風雨，平地水深數尺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Lishui had great wind and rain, and on level ground the water stood several feet deep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Daoguang 14 (1834), great wind and rain at Lishui left the flatlands several feet deep in water.

manualTranslations.zh: 十五年夏，即墨霪雨傷稼，文登、榮成大雨六十餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the fifteenth year, Jimo had incessant rain that harmed the crops; Wendeng and Rongcheng had heavy rain for more than sixty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Daoguang 15 (1835), incessant rain at Jimo damaged the crops, while Wendeng and Rongcheng endured heavy rain for more than sixty days.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月，宜城霪雨傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, Yicheng had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Daoguang 15 (1835), incessant rain at Yicheng damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十七年五月，崇陽、宜城霪雨害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, Chongyang and Yicheng had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Daoguang 17 (1837), incessant rain at Chongyang and Yicheng damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十八年六月，益都、臨淄大雨水。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighteenth year, Yidu and Linzi had great flooding rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Daoguang 18 (1838), Yidu and Linzi were struck by heavy flooding rains.

manualTranslations.zh: 十九年春，棲霞霪雨，南樂大雨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the nineteenth year, Qixia had incessant rain; Nanle had heavy rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of Daoguang 19 (1839), Qixia saw incessant rain and Nanle heavy rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 四月，招遠大雨十餘日；
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month, Zhaoyuan had heavy rain for more than ten days;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Daoguang 19 (1839), Zhaoyuan had heavy rain for more than ten days;

manualTranslations.zh: 榮成大雨，至七月不止。
manualTranslations.literal: Rongcheng had heavy rain that did not cease until the seventh month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Rongcheng heavy rain continued without cease until the seventh month.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，武進恒雨傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month, Wujin had persistent rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Daoguang 19 (1839), persistent rain at Wujin damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十年五月，邢台大雨，平地水深三尺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the twentieth year, Xingtai had heavy rain, and on level ground the water stood three feet deep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Daoguang 20 (1840), heavy rain at Xingtai left the flatlands three feet deep in water.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，平穀霪雨匝月不止。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Pinggu had incessant rain for a full month without cease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Daoguang 20 (1840), Pinggu endured incessant rain for a full month without cease.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十一年二月，武進恒雨傷麥。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-first year, Wujin had persistent rain that harmed the wheat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Daoguang 21 (1841), persistent rain at Wujin damaged the wheat.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十二年七月，麗水大雨，漂沒田廬。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-second year, Lishui had heavy rain that washed away and submerged fields and dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Daoguang 22 (1842), heavy rain at Lishui washed away and submerged fields and dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬至夜，滕縣大雨如注。
manualTranslations.literal: On the night of the winter solstice, Teng County had torrential rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the night of the winter solstice in Daoguang 22 (1842), Teng County was struck by torrential rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十三年五月，平度霪雨傷田禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-third year, Pingdu had incessant rain that harmed the field grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Daoguang 23 (1843), incessant rain at Pingdu damaged the standing grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十四年七月初九日，嵊縣大風雨，溺死男婦七十餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: On the ninth day of the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year, Sheng County had great wind and rain, and more than seventy men and women drowned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the seventh month of Daoguang 24 (1844), great wind and rain at Sheng County drowned more than seventy men and women.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬，鬆陽大雨連旬，壞田舍無數。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter, Songyang had heavy rain for successive ten-day periods, and countless fields and dwellings were destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the winter of Daoguang 24 (1844), Songyang saw heavy rain for weeks on end, destroying countless fields and dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十五年春，棗陽霪雨八十餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-fifth year, Zaoyang had incessant rain for more than eighty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of Daoguang 25 (1845), Zaoyang endured incessant rain for more than eighty days.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，滕縣大雨，平地水深數尺，人多溺死。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Teng County had heavy rain; on level ground the water stood several feet deep, and many people drowned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Daoguang 25 (1845), heavy rain at Teng County left the flatlands several feet deep in water, and many people drowned.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十六年五月，東平大雨害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-sixth year, Dongping had heavy rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Daoguang 26 (1846), heavy rain at Dongping damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，樂平霪雨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Leping had incessant rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Daoguang 26 (1846), Leping saw incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十八年，潛江自二月至七月雨不止。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Qianjiang had rain from the second month to the seventh month without cease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 28 (1848), Qianjiang saw rain from the second month through the seventh month without cease.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，光化大雨，平地水深數尺，三月始退，溺斃人無算；
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Guanghua had heavy rain, and on level ground the water stood several feet deep; only in the third month did it begin to recede, and countless people drowned;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Daoguang 28 (1848), heavy rain at Guanghua left the flatlands several feet deep in water; the flood did not begin to recede until the third month, and countless people drowned;

manualTranslations.zh: 保康霪雨兩月，壞田廬無算。
manualTranslations.literal: Baokang had incessant rain for two months, and countless fields and dwellings were destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Baokang incessant rain for two months destroyed countless fields and dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月十四日，永嘉大風雨，壞孔子廟及縣署。
manualTranslations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the seventh month, Yongjia had great wind and rain that destroyed the Confucius Temple and the county offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the seventh month of Daoguang 28 (1848), great wind and rain at Yongjia destroyed the Confucius Temple and the county offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 十九日，景寧大風雨三晝夜，壞田廬無算。
manualTranslations.literal: On the nineteenth day, Jingning had great wind and rain for three days and nights, and countless fields and dwellings were destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day, Jingning suffered three days and nights of great wind and rain, destroying countless fields and dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十九年六月，樂亭大雨傷禾稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-ninth year, Leting had heavy rain that harmed the grain crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Daoguang 29 (1849), heavy rain at Leting damaged the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，青浦霪雨五十日，湖州霪雨傷禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Qingpu had incessant rain for fifty days; Huzhou had incessant rain that harmed the grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Daoguang 29 (1849), Qingpu saw incessant rain for fifty days, and incessant rain at Huzhou damaged the grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 三十年五月二十五日，兩當暴雨，漂沒人畜。
manualTranslations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month of the thirtieth year, Liangdang had a violent rainstorm that washed away and submerged people and livestock.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month of Daoguang 30 (1850), a violent rainstorm at Liangdang washed away and submerged people and livestock.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸豐元年六月，禮縣霪雨四十餘日，傷禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Xianfeng, Li County had incessant rain for more than forty days, harming the grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xianfeng 1 (1851), Li County endured incessant rain for more than forty days, damaging the grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年，青縣大雨傷禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year, Qing County had heavy rain that harmed the grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 (1852), heavy rain at Qing County damaged the grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年四月，靜海霪雨害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, Jinghai had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xianfeng 3 (1853), incessant rain at Jinghai damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，永嘉、青田、景寧霪雨十晝夜；
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Yongjia, Qingtian, and Jingning had incessant rain for ten days and nights;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xianfeng 3 (1853), Yongjia, Qingtian, and Jingning saw incessant rain for ten days and nights;

manualTranslations.zh: 保康大雨十六日，漂沒田舍甚多；
manualTranslations.literal: Baokang had heavy rain for sixteen days, and very many fields and dwellings were washed away and submerged;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Baokang heavy rain for sixteen days washed away and submerged a great many fields and dwellings;

manualTranslations.zh: 房縣霪雨七晝夜不止，壞田舍無算。
manualTranslations.literal: Fang County had incessant rain for seven days and nights without cease, and countless fields and dwellings were destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Fang County incessant rain for seven days and nights without cease destroyed countless fields and dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，宜城大雨匝月，壞城垣一百五丈；
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Yicheng had heavy rain for a full month, and one hundred and fifty zhang of city wall were destroyed;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xianfeng 3 (1853), a full month of heavy rain at Yicheng destroyed one hundred and fifty zhang of city wall;

manualTranslations.zh: 遠州霪雨害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuanzhou had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Yuanzhou incessant rain damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年夏，湖州霪雨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year, Huzhou had incessant rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Xianfeng 4 (1854), Huzhou saw incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年七月初十日，景寧大雨如注，田廬盡壞。
manualTranslations.literal: On the tenth day of the seventh month of the fifth year, Jingning had torrential rain, and fields and dwellings were entirely destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the seventh month of Xianfeng 5 (1855), torrential rain at Jingning entirely destroyed fields and dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年六月，昌平大雨傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year, Changping had heavy rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xianfeng 6 (1856), heavy rain at Changping damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年春，崇陽霪雨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, Chongyang had incessant rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xianfeng 7 (1857), Chongyang saw incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 八年四月，海囗縣大雨損禾苗。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Hai County had heavy rain that damaged the grain seedlings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xianfeng 8 (1858), heavy rain at Hai County damaged the grain seedlings.

manualTranslations.zh: 九年五月，蘇州大雨傷禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year, Suzhou had heavy rain that harmed the grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xianfeng 9 (1859), heavy rain at Suzhou damaged the grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 十年二月，蘇州霪雨閱月。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year, Suzhou had incessant rain for a full month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xianfeng 10 (1860), Suzhou endured incessant rain for a full month.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，寧津、東光大雨傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Ningjin and Dongguang had heavy rain that damaged the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, heavy rain at Ningjin and Dongguang damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一年十一月，羅田大雨傷禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year, Luotian had heavy rain that damaged the grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Xianfeng 11 (1861), heavy rain at Luotian damaged the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 同治元年七月，蓬萊、黃縣、福山、招遠、萊陽、寧海大雨連綿，禾稼盡淹。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Tongzhi, Penglai, Huang County, Fushan, Zhaoyuan, Laiyang, and Ninghai had continuous heavy rain, and the grain crops were entirely submerged.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tongzhi 1 (1862), continuous heavy rain at Penglai, Huang County, Fushan, Zhaoyuan, Laiyang, and Ninghai wholly submerged the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年春，應城霪雨傷麥。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the second year, Yingcheng had incessant rain that damaged the wheat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tongzhi 2 (1863), incessant rain at Yingcheng damaged the wheat crop.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月，青縣大雨傷禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month, Qing County had heavy rain that damaged the grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, heavy rain at Qing County damaged the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年六月初十日，定海暴風疾雨，壞各埠船，溺死兵民無數。
manualTranslations.literal: On the tenth day of the sixth month of the third year, Dinghai had a violent wind and driving rain, destroying boats at the various wharves; soldiers and civilians drowned beyond counting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the sixth month of Tongzhi 3 (1864), a violent storm at Dinghai wrecked boats at the various wharves and drowned untold numbers of soldiers and civilians.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年六月至七月，萊陽大雨，平地水深七八尺，禾稼淹沒，房舍傾圮無算。
manualTranslations.literal: From the sixth month to the seventh month of the fourth year, Laiyang had heavy rain; on level ground the water stood seven or eight chi deep, the grain crops were submerged, and dwellings collapsed beyond counting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the sixth to the seventh month of Tongzhi 4 (1865), heavy rain at Laiyang left the flatlands seven or eight chi deep, submerged the grain crops, and destroyed untold numbers of dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年秋，魚台霪雨，水深數尺，傷禾稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year, Yutai had incessant rain; the water stood several chi deep and damaged the grain crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Tongzhi 5 (1866), incessant rain at Yutai left the water several chi deep and damaged the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年八月，鄖陽霪雨三晝夜，壞官署民房甚多。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year, Yunyang had incessant rain for three days and nights, destroying a great many government offices and civilian dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tongzhi 6 (1867), three days and nights of incessant rain at Yunyang destroyed a great many government offices and civilian dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年五月，皋蘭、金縣大雨，至七月乃止。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, Gaolan and Jin County had heavy rain, which only stopped in the seventh month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tongzhi 7 (1868), heavy rain at Gaolan and Jin County continued until the seventh month.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋，景寧大雨，傾沒田廬無算。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn, Jingning had heavy rain, washing away and submerging fields and dwellings beyond counting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That autumn, heavy rain at Jingning washed away and submerged untold numbers of fields and dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 八年春，江夏霪雨損麥。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, Jiangxia had incessant rain that damaged the wheat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tongzhi 8 (1869), incessant rain at Jiangxia damaged the wheat crop.

manualTranslations.zh: 四月，嵊縣大雨，壞田廬。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month, Sheng County had heavy rain, destroying fields and dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, heavy rain at Sheng County destroyed fields and dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 九年六月，潛江霪雨傷稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year, Qianjiang had incessant rain that damaged the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tongzhi 9 (1870), incessant rain at Qianjiang damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十年七月，東光、新樂、曲陽霪雨十餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year, Dongguang, Xinle, and Quyang had incessant rain for more than ten days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tongzhi 10 (1871), Dongguang, Xinle, and Quyang saw more than ten days of incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一年五月，東平霪雨害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year, Dongping had incessant rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tongzhi 11 (1872), incessant rain at Dongping damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一月，青縣大雨害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month, Qing County had heavy rain that harmed the crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, heavy rain at Qing County damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二年七月，太平大風雨，壞城垣數十丈，民房數百間。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the twelfth year, Taiping had a great wind and rain, destroying several tens of zhang of city wall and several hundred civilian dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tongzhi 12 (1873), a violent storm at Taiping destroyed several tens of zhang of city wall and several hundred homes.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月，化平廳霪雨不止，壞民舍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, Huaping Subprefecture had incessant rain that would not stop, destroying civilian dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, unceasing incessant rain at Huaping Subprefecture destroyed civilian dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 光緒元年六月，日照大風雨，平地水深數尺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Guangxu, Rizhao had a great wind and rain; on level ground the water stood several chi deep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guangxu 1 (1875), a violent storm at Rizhao left the flatlands several chi deep.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年六月初八日，黃岩大風雨，拔木壞屋，田禾淹沒殆盡。
manualTranslations.literal: On the eighth day of the sixth month of the second year, Huangyan had a great wind and rain, uprooting trees and destroying houses; the field grain was nearly entirely submerged.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the sixth month of Guangxu 2 (1876), a violent storm at Huangyan uprooted trees, destroyed houses, and nearly wholly submerged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年六月，高陵大雨如注，平地水深三尺，田禾盡沒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, Gaoling had heavy rain pouring down; on level ground the water stood three chi deep, and the field grain was entirely submerged.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guangxu 3 (1877), rain pouring down at Gaoling left the flatlands three chi deep and wholly submerged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年九月，東平大雨傷禾稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year, Dongping had heavy rain that damaged the grain crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Guangxu 4 (1878), heavy rain at Dongping damaged the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年五月，登州各屬大雨四十餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, the various subordinate districts of Dengzhou had heavy rain for more than forty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Guangxu 5 (1879), the various subordinate districts of Dengzhou saw more than forty days of heavy rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月二十一日，永嘉大風雨，壞官廳民居。
manualTranslations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the sixth month, Yongjia had a great wind and rain, destroying government offices and civilian dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the sixth month, a violent storm at Yongjia destroyed government offices and civilian dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月，莘縣霪雨十日方止。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, Shen County had incessant rain for ten days before it stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, incessant rain at Shen County continued for ten days before it stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年三月，福山大雨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, Fushan had heavy rain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guangxu 6 (1880), Fushan saw heavy rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年秋，灤州霪雨連旬。
manualTranslations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year, Luanzhou had incessant rain for more than ten days in succession.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Guangxu 7 (1881), Luanzhou saw more than ten days of incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 八年秋，宜城霪雨傷禾稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year, Yicheng had incessant rain that damaged the grain crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Guangxu 8 (1882), incessant rain at Yicheng damaged the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬，均州霪雨彌月。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter, Junzhou had incessant rain for a full month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That winter, Junzhou endured a full month of incessant rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 九年六月，化平廳大雨，水深四五尺，傷禾稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year, Huaping Subprefecture had heavy rain; the water stood four or five chi deep and damaged the grain crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guangxu 9 (1883), heavy rain at Huaping Subprefecture left the water four or five chi deep and damaged the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十年八月，太平大雨，衝沒廬舍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year, Taiping had heavy rain, washing away and submerging dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Guangxu 10 (1884), heavy rain at Taiping washed away and submerged dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二年七月十四日，太平大風雨，二十日始止。
manualTranslations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the seventh month of the twelfth year, Taiping had a great wind and rain, which only stopped on the twentieth day.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the seventh month of Guangxu 12 (1886), a violent storm at Taiping continued until the twentieth day before it stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 十三年閏四月，德安大雨三日，水高五六尺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of the thirteenth year, De'an had heavy rain for three days; the water stood five or six chi high.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of Guangxu 13 (1887), three days of heavy rain at De'an left the water five or six chi deep.

manualTranslations.zh: 十五年七月二十六日夜，德安大雨如注，城崩百四十餘丈，淹斃男婦七十餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: On the night of the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month of the fifteenth year, De'an had heavy rain pouring down; more than one hundred and forty zhang of city wall collapsed, and more than seventy men and women were drowned to death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the night of the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month of Guangxu 15 (1889), rain pouring down at De'an collapsed more than one hundred and forty zhang of city wall and drowned more than seventy men and women.

manualTranslations.zh: 十六年六月，山丹驟雨壞城郭。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixteenth year, Shandan had sudden rain that destroyed the city walls and suburbs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guangxu 16 (1890), sudden rain at Shandan destroyed the city walls and suburbs.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十二年春，寧津大雨壞民居。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year, Ningjin had heavy rain that destroyed civilian dwellings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of Guangxu 22 (1896), heavy rain at Ningjin destroyed civilian dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十五年七月，秦安大雨連旬。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year, Qin'an had heavy rain for more than ten days in succession.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Guangxu 25 (1899), Qin'an saw more than ten days of heavy rain.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十七年七月，山丹大雨，平地水深數尺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year, Shandan had heavy rain; on level ground the water stood several chi deep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Guangxu 27 (1901), heavy rain at Shandan left the flatlands several chi deep.

manualTranslations.zh: 雍正三年七月，靈川五都廖家塘有村民同眾入山砍竹不歸，一百四十餘日始抵家，所言多不經。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of Yongzheng 3, at Liaojia Pond in Wudu, Lingchuan, a villager entered the mountains with others to cut bamboo and did not return; only after more than one hundred and forty days did he reach home, and much of what he said was absurd.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yongzheng 3 (1725), at Liaojia Pond in Wudu, Lingchuan, a villager went into the mountains with others to cut bamboo and did not return; only after more than one hundred and forty days did he reach home, and much of what he told was fantastic and beyond belief.

manualTranslations.zh: 道光十七年，崇陽鄉民好服尖頭帽鞋，站步不穩，識者謂之服妖。
manualTranslations.literal: In Daoguang 17, rural folk in Chongyang liked to wear pointed caps and shoes; standing and walking were unsteady, and those who understood called it a garment prodigy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 17 (1837), rural folk in Chongyang took to wearing pointed caps and shoes; they could not stand or walk steadily, and knowing observers called it strange dress—a garment prodigy.

manualTranslations.zh: 順治二年十二月，上海小南門薑姓家雞翼下各生一爪。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month of Shunzhi 2, at the Jiang family's home by Xiaonan Gate in Shanghai, under each wing of a chicken grew one claw.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Shunzhi 2 (1645), at the Jiang family's home by Xiaonan Gate in Shanghai, a claw grew under each wing of a chicken.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年八月，揭陽牝雞鳴數日乃已。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, Jieyang had a hen crow for several days before it stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Shunzhi 3 (1646), a hen at Jieyang crowed for several days before it stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年四月，淄川民間訛言雞兩翅生骨，食之殺人，驗之果然。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, among the common folk of Zichuan a rumor spread that when a chicken's two wings grew bone, eating it would kill a person; on investigation it proved true.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 4 (1647), a rumor spread among the common folk of Zichuan that when a chicken's two wings grew bone, eating it would kill a person; on investigation this proved true.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月，忠州民家殺雞，腹內有一嬰兒；
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month, at a commoner's home in Zhongzhou a chicken was slaughtered, and inside its belly was an infant;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, at a commoner's home in Zhongzhou a chicken was slaughtered, and inside its belly was an infant;

manualTranslations.zh: 漢陽雞翅生爪。
manualTranslations.literal: At Hanyang, chicken wings grew claws.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Hanyang, chicken wings grew claws.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年，崇明民家雞翼中生爪；
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year, at a commoner's home in Chongming claws grew in the chicken wings;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 (1648), at a commoner's home in Chongming, claws grew in the chicken wings;

manualTranslations.zh: 巫山民間雞翅端皆生一爪如距；
manualTranslations.literal: Among the common folk of Wushan, at the tips of chicken wings each grew one claw like a spur;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among the common folk of Wushan, at the tips of chicken wings each grew one claw like a spur;

manualTranslations.zh: 杭州民家雞生四足；
manualTranslations.literal: At a commoner's home in Hangzhou, a chicken was born with four feet;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At a commoner's home in Hangzhou, a chicken was born with four feet;

manualTranslations.zh: 湖州民家雞生四翼，能飛。
manualTranslations.literal: At a commoner's home in Huzhou, a chicken was born with four wings and could fly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At a commoner's home in Huzhou, a chicken was born with four wings and could fly.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一年，合肥鄭家莊產一雞，三嘴、三眼、三翼、三足，色黃，比三日死。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh year, at Zhengjiazhuang in Hefei a chicken was born with three beaks, three eyes, three wings, and three feet; it was yellow in color and died after three days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 (1654), at Zhengjiazhuang in Hefei a chicken was born with three beaks, three eyes, three wings, and three feet; it was yellow in color and died after three days.

manualTranslations.zh: 十六年，崇明民家雄雞生二卵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixteenth year, at a Chongming commoner's home a rooster laid two eggs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 (1659), a rooster at a commoner's home in Chongming laid two eggs.

manualTranslations.zh: 十八年，鎮澤民家雄雞生卵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighteenth year, at a Zhenze commoner's home a rooster laid an egg.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 (1661), a rooster at a commoner's home in Zhenze laid an egg.

manualTranslations.zh: 康熙十一年，廣平民家抱一雛雞，四足四翼。
manualTranslations.literal: In Kangxi 11, at a Guangping commoner's home a chick was hatched with four legs and four wings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 (1672), a commoner's home in Guangping hatched a chick with four legs and four wings.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二年，平湖民家雞生四足四翼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth year, at a Pinghu commoner's home a chicken was born with four legs and four wings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 (1673), a chicken at a commoner's home in Pinghu was born with four legs and four wings.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十二年，迎春鄉民間雌雞化為雄。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-second year, among the common people of Yingchun township a hen transformed into a rooster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 (1683), among the common people of Yingchun township a hen transformed into a rooster.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十三年，麻城民田姓家雞生一卵，膜內皆有紋，其色朱；
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-third year, at the home of a commoner surnamed Tian in Macheng a chicken laid an egg; inside the membrane there were patterns on all sides, their color vermilion;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23 (1684), a chicken at the home of a commoner surnamed Tian in Macheng laid an egg; inside the membrane were vermilion patterns throughout;

manualTranslations.zh: 後七日又生一卵，有圖；
manualTranslations.literal: Seven days later it laid another egg, which had a design;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seven days later it laid another egg bearing a design;

manualTranslations.zh: 又數日，毛成五色，飛去。
manualTranslations.literal: After several more days, its feathers became five colors, and it flew away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Several days later its feathers turned five colors, and it flew away.

manualTranslations.zh: 雍正二年，麻城雞翅遍生人指。
manualTranslations.literal: In Yongzheng 2, in Macheng chicken wings all over grew human fingers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 (1724), chicken wings throughout Macheng grew human fingers.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年，通州雌雞化為雄。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year, at Tongzhou a hen transformed into a rooster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 (1727), a hen at Tongzhou transformed into a rooster.

manualTranslations.zh: 乾隆三十九年冬，慶元雄雞自斷其尾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the winter of Qianlong 39, at Qingyuan a rooster severed its own tail.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the winter of Qianlong 39 (1774), a rooster in Qingyuan severed its own tail.

manualTranslations.zh: 六十年，貴陽民家雄雞生二卵，色赤甚鮮。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixtieth year, at a Guiyang commoner's home a rooster laid two eggs, their color very bright red.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 60 (1795), a rooster at a commoner's home in Guiyang laid two eggs of a vivid red color.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉慶十一年，樂清民家雞生四足。
manualTranslations.literal: In Jiaqing 11, at a Yueqing commoner's home a chicken was born with four legs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 11 (1806), a chicken at a commoner's home in Yueqing was born with four legs.

manualTranslations.zh: 十七年，宜昌民間雞生四足，後二足微短，行不著地；
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventeenth year, among the common people of Yichang chickens were born with four legs; the rear two legs were slightly short, and when walking they did not touch the ground;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 17 (1812), chickens among the common people of Yichang were born with four legs; the hind pair were slightly short and did not reach the ground when walking;

manualTranslations.zh: 又有三足者，其一生於尾下，如鼎足然。
manualTranslations.literal: There were also three-legged ones; one leg grew beneath the tail, like a tripod's legs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There were also three-legged birds, one leg growing beneath the tail like a tripod stand.

manualTranslations.zh: 道光元年秋，青浦民家雞翼兩旁生爪；
manualTranslations.literal: In the autumn of Daoguang 1, at a Qingpu commoner's home a chicken's wings on both sides grew claws;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Daoguang 1 (1821), a chicken at a commoner's home in Qingpu grew claws on both sides of its wings;

manualTranslations.zh: 湖州民家雞兩翅皆生五爪，飛去；
manualTranslations.literal: At a Huzhou commoner's home a chicken's two wings each grew five claws, and it flew away;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At a commoner's home in Huzhou a chicken's two wings each sprouted five claws, then flew away;

manualTranslations.zh: 永嘉雞翅生爪，食之殺人。
manualTranslations.literal: In Yongjia chicken wings grew claws; eating them killed people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yongjia chickens grew claws on their wings; eating them killed people.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二年，永嘉民家雞四足，不能啼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth year, at a Yongjia commoner's home a chicken had four legs and could not crow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12 (1832), a chicken at a commoner's home in Yongjia had four legs and could not crow.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十二年，良鄉民家牝雞化為雄，能鳴，無距。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-second year, at a Liangxiang commoner's home a hen transformed into a rooster; it could crow but had no spur.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 22 (1842), a hen at a commoner's home in Liangxiang transformed into a rooster; it could crow but had no spur.

manualTranslations.zh: 三十年六月，蘄水縣民家雌雞化為雄，冠距儼然，唯啼聲微弱。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirtieth year, at a Qishui County commoner's home a hen transformed into a rooster; comb and spur were fully formed, only the crow was faint.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Daoguang 30 (1850), a hen at a commoner's home in Qishui County transformed into a rooster with a fully formed comb and spur, though its crow was faint.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸豐五年，隨州民家雄雞生卵。
manualTranslations.literal: In Xianfeng 5, at a Suizhou commoner's home a rooster laid an egg.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 5 (1855), a rooster at a commoner's home in Suizhou laid an egg.

manualTranslations.zh: 同治元年六月，定遠廳民家雞生三足。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of Tongzhi 1, at a Dingyuan Sub-prefecture commoner's home a chicken was born with three legs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tongzhi 1 (1862), a chicken at a commoner's home in Dingyuan Sub-prefecture was born with three legs.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年，鍾祥民家雛雞生三翅。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth year, at a Zhongxiang commoner's home a chick was born with three wings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 6 (1867), a chick at a commoner's home in Zhongxiang was born with three wings.

manualTranslations.zh: 光緒九年，興山民家雌雞化為雄。
manualTranslations.literal: In Guangxu 9, at a Xingshan commoner's home a hen transformed into a rooster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 (1883), a hen at a commoner's home in Xingshan transformed into a rooster.

manualTranslations.zh: 三十年，寧州民家雞生三足，後一足微短，行不著地。
manualTranslations.literal: In the thirtieth year, at a Ningzhou commoner's home a chicken was born with three legs; the rear leg was slightly short, and when walking it did not touch the ground.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 30 (1904), a chicken at a commoner's home in Ningzhou was born with three legs; the hind leg was slightly short and did not reach the ground when walking.

manualTranslations.zh: 康熙二十年五月，巴東鼠食麥，色赤，尾大；
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of Kangxi 20, at Badong rats ate wheat; they were red in color, with large tails;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kangxi 20 (1681), at Badong rats ate wheat; they were red in color and had large tails;

manualTranslations.zh: 江陵鼠災，食禾殆盡。
manualTranslations.literal: At Jiangling there was a rat calamity, and they ate the grain almost entirely.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Jiangling a rat calamity ate the grain crops almost entirely.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十一年，西寧鼠食禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-first year, at Xining rats ate grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 21 (1682), rats at Xining ate the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十二年夏，崇陽田鼠結巢於禾麻之上。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-second year, at Chongyang field rats built nests on top of the grain and hemp.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kangxi 22 (1683), field rats at Chongyang built nests atop the grain and hemp.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十八年，黃岡鼠食禾，及秋，化為魚。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, at Huanggang rats ate grain; by autumn they transformed into fish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 28 (1689), rats at Huanggang ate the grain crops; by autumn they had transformed into fish.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十九年，孝感鼠食稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, at Xiaogan rats ate crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 (1690), rats at Xiaogan ate the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 四十二年，西鄉、定遠廳遍地生五色鼠。
manualTranslations.literal: In the forty-second year, at Xixiang and Dingyuan Sub-prefecture five-colored rats were born everywhere throughout the land.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 42 (1703), five-colored rats appeared everywhere throughout Xixiang and Dingyuan Sub-prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 四十七年，黃濟鼠食禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, at Huangji rats ate grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 47 (1708), rats at Huangji ate the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 四十八年七月，崖州有鼠千萬啣尾渡江。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the forty-eighth year, at Yazhou there were tens of millions of rats holding tails in their mouths crossing the river.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kangxi 48 (1709), tens of millions of rats at Yazhou crossed a river linked tail-to-tail.

manualTranslations.zh: 五十二年五月，高淳、丹陽有鼠無數，食禾殆盡。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifty-second year, at Gaochun and Danyang there were rats beyond counting, and they ate the grain almost entirely.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kangxi 52 (1713), countless rats at Gaochun and Danyang ate the grain crops almost entirely.

manualTranslations.zh: 六十一年夏，延安田鼠食稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the sixty-first year, at Yan'an field rats ate crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kangxi 61 (1722), field rats at Yan'an ate the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋，安定黑鼠為災，食禾殆盡，有鄉民掘地得一鼠，身後半蝦蟆形，疑其所化也；
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn, at Anding black rats became a calamity and ate the grain almost entirely; a countryman digging in the ground obtained one rat, its rear half in the shape of a toad— it was suspected to be what they had transformed into;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That autumn, black rats at Anding wrought disaster and ate the grain crops almost entirely; a villager digging in the earth found one rat whose rear half was shaped like a toad, suspected to be what they had become;

manualTranslations.zh: 清澗黃鼠食苗殆盡；
manualTranslations.literal: At Qingjian yellow rats ate seedlings almost entirely;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Qingjian yellow rats ate the seedlings almost entirely;

manualTranslations.zh: 葭州田鼠食苗。
manualTranslations.literal: At Jiazhou field rats ate seedlings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Field rats at Jiazhou ate the seedlings.

manualTranslations.zh: 雍正五年十一月，銅陵群鼠銜尾渡江。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month of Yongzheng 5, at Tongling a swarm of rats holding tails in their mouths crossed the river.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yongzheng 5 (1727), a swarm of rats at Tongling crossed a river linked tail-to-tail.

manualTranslations.zh: 乾隆元年，文縣鼠害稼。
manualTranslations.literal: In Qianlong 1, at Wen County rats harmed crops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 (1736), rats at Wen County damaged the crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年四月，什邡縣白鼠晝見羅寺經堂中，異香滿室。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, at Shifang County a white rat appeared by day in the scripture hall of Luosi Temple, and a strange fragrance filled the room.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Qianlong 4 (1739), a white rat appeared in daylight in the scripture hall of Luosi Temple in Shifang County, and a strange fragrance filled the room.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋，彭澤群鼠銜尾渡江，食禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn, at Pengze a swarm of rats holding tails in their mouths crossed the river and ate grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That autumn, a swarm of rats at Pengze crossed a river linked tail-to-tail and ate the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 十四年二月，中衛田鼠食麥。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year, at Zhongwei field rats ate wheat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Qianlong 14 (1749), field rats at Zhongwei ate wheat.

manualTranslations.zh: 十八年，池州田鼠叢生，忽入水化為魚。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighteenth year, at Chizhou field rats proliferated; suddenly entering the water they transformed into fish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 18 (1753), field rats at Chizhou proliferated; entering the water they suddenly transformed into fish.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十五年五月，池州田鼠叢生，有赤鷹來食之，遂滅。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-fifth year, at Chizhou field rats proliferated; a red hawk came and ate them, and they were exterminated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Qianlong 25 (1760), field rats at Chizhou proliferated; a red hawk came and devoured them until they were gone.

manualTranslations.zh: 道光四年，高淳鼠食麥。
manualTranslations.literal: In Daoguang 4, at Gaochun rats ate wheat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 4 (1824), rats at Gaochun ate wheat.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十八年五月，沔陽常平倉忽有鼠數千頭在梁上，移時方散。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-eighth year, at Mianyang in the Ever-Normal Granary there were suddenly several thousand rats on the beams; after a while they then dispersed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Daoguang 28 (1848), several thousand rats suddenly appeared on the beams of the Ever-Normal Granary at Mianyang and dispersed only after some time.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸豐元年六月，德化群鼠銜尾渡江。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of Xianfeng 1, at Dehua a swarm of rats holding tails in their mouths crossed the river.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xianfeng 1 (1851), a swarm of rats at Dehua crossed a river linked tail-to-tail.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年，襄陽群鼠食禾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year, at Xiangyang a swarm of rats ate grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 4 (1854), swarms of rats at Xiangyang ate the grain crops.

manualTranslations.zh: 同治七年，山丹田鼠食苗。
manualTranslations.literal: In Tongzhi 7, at Shandan field rats ate seedlings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 7 (1868), field rats at Shandan ate the seedlings.

manualTranslations.zh: 九年二月，皋蘭土塊化為鼠。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year, at Gaolan clods of earth transformed into rats.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tongzhi 9 (1870), clods of earth at Gaolan transformed into rats.
